answer: A new identity's attested earnings convert to tokens only when backed by payments from counterparties that are themselves net payers, so an operator cannot mint credit by shuffling coins inside a closed clique. Payout fees scale with how tightly the payer graph clusters: a lone agent sells across the wide grove of independent buyers and pays the base rate, while a ring of n clones trading only with itself climbs a terrace of rising multiplier tiers, its cost growing with every added pair, not every added name. An orchard of a thousand socks is expensive; one honest seller is cheap.
